transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just feel worn out all the time. It's like... even after a full night in bed, my body just feels like it's made of sandbags. Um, just getting through my workday, or honestly even just folding the laundry at home, it takes absolutely everything I have right now.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly or seem to stop breathing or gasp for air while you're asleep?
No, nobody has ever mentioned anything like that to me. I don't think I snore, and I haven't been told I gasp for air or stop breathing. I just... wake up still feeling completely exhausted.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or found yourself feeling down or hopeless most of the day?

Yeah, I have. Most days I wake up with this... heavy, flat feeling right in my chest. I'll just sit at the kitchen table, staring out at the yard, and I just feel like there is no good version of the future coming. It's just a very down, hopeless feeling that kind of sticks with me most of the day.
How long have you been feeling this way—the low mood and exhaustion—has it been going on for two weeks or more, or longer than that?
It's definitely been longer than two weeks. I'd say... this whole depressed, slowed-down, exhausted feeling has been going on most days for about the past two months now.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold or having trouble tolerating cold temperatures compared to before?
No, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed feeling any colder than usual. My temperature seems fine, so... no, that hasn't been an issue for me.
Have you noticed being unusually thirsty or needing to urinate more often than usual recently?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I drink about the same amount of water I always do, and... no, I haven't been going to the bathroom any more than normal.
Have you ever had a similar period of low mood and exhaustion like this before, at any earlier point in your life?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had days where I felt tired or down, like anyone else, but... nothing like this. This is the first time it's been this bad and lasted this long.
Have you noticed feeling unusually short of breath, lightheaded, or dizzy when you're active, or has anyone commented that you look pale?

No, I haven't had any issues with that. I mean, I'm not doing a whole lot of physical activity right now anyway, but... no, no dizziness or feeling out of breath when I do move around. And nobody's mentioned me looking pale, either.
Have you noticed that even mild physical or mental exertion leaves you feeling significantly worse afterward, with symptoms that can last for a day or more?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm already pretty exhausted most of the time right now, but doing something mild doesn't really make me crash for a day or two afterward. It's just... a steady kind of tired. So, no, I haven't noticed it getting significantly worse just from a little bit of effort.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off not being alive?

Well, um... yes, actually. I wouldn't say I want to hurt myself, but... especially late at night, I catch myself thinking that my husband might just be better off without me. I haven't made any kind of plan or anything like that, but... the thought just keeps coming back. It happens enough that it really scares me.

Has this exhaustion and low mood made it difficult to keep up with your usual responsibilities, like going to work or managing daily tasks, or have you still been able to function despite the struggle?

Yes, it definitely has. I've actually fallen behind on my client reports. I just... I've started avoiding my friends, too, and I stopped doing the outdoor routines that usually keep me steady. Right now, pretty much all my energy just goes into getting through work and handling the bare basics at home. Anything beyond that is just... it's not happening right now.
Have you found it difficult to manage basic daily self-care, like bathing, eating regularly, or getting out of bed, because of how you've been feeling?

No, I haven't really had trouble with that stuff. I mean, I still get up and take a shower, and I'm eating normally. It's not like I'm stuck in bed all day. I just... I don't have the energy for anything extra, but the basic things like brushing my teeth and getting dressed, I can still manage those fine.
How often are you having these thoughts that your husband would be better off without you—would you say it's just occasional, or is it happening every day or almost constantly?

I haven't really kept track of the exact days, to be honest. It's... I wouldn't say it's constantly playing in my head, but I'm not really sure if it's every single day, either. It just mostly creeps in at night when things get quiet. I don't know the exact frequency, it just feels like it happens enough to really bother me.
When you have these thoughts about your husband being better off without you, do you ever feel an urge to act on them, or have you thought about how you might do something to harm yourself?

No, I haven't felt an urge to actually do anything. It's just... like I mentioned, late at night I catch myself thinking my husband might be better off without me. I haven't thought about how I would harm myself, and I definitely haven't made a plan or anything like that. But... even without a plan, the fact that the thought just keeps coming back enough to notice... it really scares me.

inference.note: Thyroid, anemia, diabetes, sleep apnea, and CFS/PEM features have been ruled out through negative review of systems. Patient endorses 2 months of depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, hopelessness, passive suicidal ideation, and functional impairment (falling behind at work, social withdrawal) without prior episodes or psychotic features, consistent with a single moderate depressive episode.

opening_question.intent: Identify the primary reason for the visit today
opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a 2-month history of depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue/low energy, hopelessness, passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent, and social withdrawal, along with functional impairment (falling behind at work, avoiding friends, stopping usual activities). No prior depressive episodes reported, ruling out recurrent depressive disorder (F33). Basic self-care remains intact and there are no psychotic features, and the presentation does not reach severe intensity given preserved functioning in basic domains and lack of active suicidal planning, supporting a moderate rather than severe episode. Medical causes (thyroid dysfunction, diabetes, sleep apnea, anemia, chronic fatigue syndrome/ME) were screened for and denied, supporting a primary mood disorder diagnosis.

confirmed_symptoms: Depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day
Loss of interest/pleasure in previously enjoyed activities (outdoor routines, socializing)
Persistent fatigue and low energy despite adequate sleep
Feelings of hopelessness about the future
Passive suicidal ideation ('husband would be better off without me') without plan or intent

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms present most days for approximately 2 months, exceeding the minimum 2-week threshold for a depressive episode.
additional_requirements: No prior depressive episodes reported, consistent with single episode rather than recurrent disorder
Basic self-care (bathing, eating, dressing) preserved, supporting moderate rather than severe severity
Medical/organic causes (thyroid dysfunction, diabetes, sleep apnea, anemia, ME/CFS) screened and ruled out via review of systems
Suicidal ideation is passive, without plan or intent, though present and distressing to patient
